style: Indie rock, English male lead vocal, jangly electric guitars, live bass and drums, Hammond organ, mid tempo 92 BPM, bittersweet verse and big anthemic chorus, warm analog production
lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
The radio next door went quiet
and the patio smells like rain
You left the kettle and the notebook
and a list of songs without an end

[Pre-Chorus]
And I don't know if I'm coming back
and I don't know if I should wait
but the river keeps on talking to itself

[Chorus]
Dance with me until the sun comes up
let the night keep all our secrets
if the world gets too big, darling
come back to my street, come back to my voice

[Verse 2]
Sunday mornings live down at the corner
the game is playing on the pavement
Your laugh slips between the passing cars
and the traffic light leaves us on amber

[Pre-Chorus]
And I don't know if I'm coming back
and I don't know if I should wait
but the river keeps on talking to itself

[Chorus]
Dance with me until the sun comes up
let the night keep all our secrets
if the world gets too big, darling
come back to my street, come back to my voice

[Bridge]
If you go, leave the door open
summer always finds its way back here
and even if the corner changes names
your song is going to find me

[Chorus]
Dance with me until the sun comes up
let the night keep all our secrets
if the world gets too big, darling
come back to my street, come back to my voice

[Outro]
Come back to my voice
come back to my voice
